TUBERCULOSIS 
Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative organism of tubercu-
losis (TB), is an intracellular bacterial parasite, has a slow rate 
of growth, is an obligate aerobe, and induces a granulomatous 
response in the tissues of a normal host. 
Even though TB is not as common in the United States as 
in some other countries, there has been a resurgence associ-
ated with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and drug-
resistant forms of TB (see Chapter 37). The World Health 
Organization (WHO) estimates approximately 630,000 
cases of TB worldwide. In 2013 TB remained a major health 
concern with resistance to multidrug-resistant TB on the 
rise. Increase in relocation of this population of patients, 
the HIV pandemic, and increase in multidrug-resistant TB 
poses global concerns in the management of TB (Abubakar 
et al, 2013).
